name: Wilhelm Barthlott
summary: German botanist known for discovering the self-cleaning properties of lotus leaves and coining the Lotus-Effect.

name: Christoph Neinhuis
summary: Botanist and author of the commentary, former student assistant in Barthlott's group.

name: University of Heidelberg
aliases: Institute for Botany of the University of Heidelberg
summary: German university where Barthlott began his Ph.D. studies in the 1970s.

name: University of Bonn
summary: German university where Barthlott was appointed professor for botany.

name: Lotus-Effect
summary: Trademark and concept describing self-cleaning properties of rough hydrophobic surfaces inspired by lotus leaves.

name: Planta
summary: Scientific journal where the seminal paper on self-cleaning surfaces was published in 1997.

name: Andreas Sievers
summary: Former editor who helped publish Barthlott's paper in Planta.

name: Nelumbo nucifera
summary: Plant species whose leaves exhibited the self-cleaning properties studied by Barthlott.

name: PTFE
summary: Material used in early technical demonstrators to replicate lotus surface roughness.
